models.name: discussion_board_guests
models.description:
Temporary guest accounts identified by device fingerprint for tracking unauthenticated visitors.

Guest actors represent unauthenticated visitors who browse the discussion board without logging in. They are tracked via device fingerprint rather than traditional credentials like email and password.

Key characteristics:
- No authentication credentials (email/password) required
- Device fingerprint provides anonymous identification
- Read-only access to public content (sections, articles, comments)
- Cannot create, edit, or delete any content
- Sessions tracked through {@link discussion_board_guest_sessions} table

Relationships:- Has many sessions via {@link discussion_board_guest_sessions.guest_id}

This actor table serves as the foundation for tracking guest activity while maintaining privacy without requiring authentication.

plainFields.name: device_fingerprint
plainFields.description: Unique device fingerprint for identifying anonymous visitors without requiring authentication credentials. Used for tracking guest sessions across page views.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was soft deleted. Null if the account is active.

models.name: discussion_board_guest_sessions
models.description:
Session tracking for guest actors, recording temporary access tokens with connection metadata.

Guest sessions capture the context of unauthenticated visitor access, including IP address for security tracking, the current page URL (href), and referrer information. Each session has a defined expiration time to limit the validity of guest access tokens.

Relationships:
- Belongs to {@link discussion_board_guests} as the parent actor record

Sessions are append-only records used for security auditing and temporary access management. Unlike authenticated member sessions, guest sessions do not require password reset functionality.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_guest_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the guest actor who owns this session. {@link discussion_board_guests.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the guest session was initiated. Used for security tracking and fraud prevention.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: The URL page the guest was viewing when the session was created. Captures navigation context for analytics.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: The URL from which the guest navigated to the current page. Used for traffic source analysis and tracking.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest session was created. Used for session lifecycle management and security auditing.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest session expires. Sessions must have explicit expiration for security - no indefinite sessions allowed.

models.name: discussion_board_members
models.description:
Registered member accounts with email/password authentication, profile information (display name, bio), and account status.

Members are authenticated discussion board participants who can create articles with attachments and tags, write comments, edit/delete their own content, manage their profile, submit admin requests, and view other member profiles. Each member has a unique email address for login identification, a securely hashed password, and optional profile details (display name, bio). Account status includes an active/banned flag with an optional ban reason for administrative moderation.

Relationships:
- Has many {@link discussion_board_articles} as author
- Has many {@link discussion_board_comments} as author
- Has many {@link discussion_board_admin_requests} as requester
- Has many {@link discussion_board_member_sessions} for session tracking

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used as the primary identifier for authentication and login. Must be unique across all member accounts.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Securely hashed password for authentication. Stored using bcrypt or similar secure hashing algorithm. Never stored in plain text.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Public display name shown on profile and all contributions (articles, comments). Can be modified by the member at any time.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: Optional biographical text for member profile. Members can use this to describe themselves to other users.

plainFields.name: banned
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether the member account is currently banned. Banned members cannot log in or access member-only features. Defaults to false.

plainFields.name: ban_reason
plainFields.description: Explanation for why the member was banned. Only set when banned is true. Administrators must provide a reason when banning a member.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was created. Set automatically upon registration.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was last modified. Updated automatically when profile fields change.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was soft-deleted. Null if account is active. Account deletion is irreversible.

models.name: discussion_board_member_sessions
models.description: Member login sessions tracking JWT authentication with connection metadata for auditing and security. Each session belongs to exactly one member and maintains an expiration timestamp. When a new session is created for a member with an existing active session, the previous session is terminated to enforce the single active session policy. Sessions are validated on each request by checking the expiration and member's ban status.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: The member who owns this session. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Client IP address from which the login originated, used for security auditing and session validation.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: The URL path where the login was initiated, providing context for the authentication request.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: The HTTP referrer header value provided by the client, if available.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created, marking the start of the authentication period.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires. Must be set to enforce session lifetime limits. Active sessions have expired_at greater than current time.

models.name: discussion_board_member_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for member account recovery with expiration tracking.

This table stores time-limited tokens that allow members to reset their passwords through an email-based recovery flow. Each token is unique and expires after a defined period for security purposes.

Key characteristics:
- Tokens are one-time-use and unique across the system
- Expiration is mandatory (non-null expired_at) for security
- Multiple tokens can exist per member over time (history of reset requests)
- Tokens are invalidated after use or expiration

Relationships:
- Each reset token belongs to exactly one {@link discussion_board_members.member}
- Referenced during the password reset verification process

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: The member who requested this password reset. {@link discussion_board_members.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique password reset token generated for secure account recovery. This cryptographically secure token is sent to the member's email and must be presented to complete the password reset process.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was generated. Used for audit trail and token age verification.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this reset token expires. After this time, the token is invalid and a new reset request must be made. Mandatory for security - tokens must have a defined lifetime.

models.name: discussion_board_admins
models.description:
Administrator accounts with email/password authentication and elevated platform privileges.

This table stores the core identity and authentication credentials for administrator users, who have extended capabilities beyond regular members including content moderation, user management, and administrative request processing. Administrators are classified into two grades: regular administrators who can manage content and users, and super administrators who additionally manage administrator requests and grade assignments.

Administrators authenticate through email and password, establishing sessions tracked in {@link discussion_board_admin_sessions}. Password reset flows are managed through {@link discussion_board_admin_password_resets}, and all administrative actions are logged in {@link discussion_board_admin_audit_logs} for audit compliance.

Administrators retain all member capabilities including article creation, commenting, and profile management. The grade field determines the scope of administrative privileges available to each user. Super administrators can promote regular administrators to super status and demote other super administrators to regular status, but cannot demote themselves.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Administrator's email address used as unique identifier for authentication. Must be a valid email format and unique across all administrator accounts.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Securely hashed password for authentication. Stored using strong cryptographic hashing algorithm, never in plain text.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Administrator's display name shown on their profile and associated content. Can be modified by the administrator at any time.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: Optional biographical text displayed on the administrator's profile. May be empty or null if not provided.

plainFields.name: grade
plainFields.description: Administrator privilege level. Valid values: 'regular' (standard admin capabilities including content moderation and user banning) or 'super' (all regular capabilities plus administrator request approval and grade management).

plainFields.name: banned_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator was banned from the platform. Null indicates the account is not banned. Banned administrators cannot authenticate or access the platform.

plainFields.name: ban_reason
plainFields.description: Reason recorded when an administrator is banned. Only set when banned_at is not null. Required for transparency in administrative actions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was soft-deleted. Null for active accounts. When set, the account is considered deleted but retained for audit purposes.

models.name: discussion_board_admin_sessions
models.description:
Administrator login sessions tracking JWT authentication tokens and connection metadata for security auditing.

Each session represents an authenticated admin connection with IP address, access URL, and referrer information. Sessions are created upon successful login and terminated through logout, expiration, or when a new session replaces an existing one (single session policy). The expired_at timestamp supports both access token expiration validation and refresh token lifecycle management.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who owns this session. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the admin logged in, captured for security auditing and session validation.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL path the admin was accessing when the session was created, useful for redirecting after authentication.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP referrer header from the login request, providing context about how the admin arrived at the login page.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created upon successful authentication.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires, used for both access token validation and refresh token lifecycle management. Sessions past this time require re-authentication.

models.name: discussion_board_admin_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for administrator account recovery with secure single-use tokens and expiration tracking.

When an administrator requests a password reset, a unique token is generated and stored with an expiration timestamp. The token allows the administrator to securely reset their password without being logged in. Tokens are invalidated after use or upon expiration.

This table maintains a one-to-many relationship with {@link discussion_board_admins}, allowing the system to track reset request history while typically ensuring only one active token per administrator at a time through application logic.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_admin_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator account requesting password reset. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique cryptographic token for password reset verification. This secure random string is sent to the administrator's email and must be presented to complete the password reset process.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp for the reset token. After this time, the token becomes invalid and a new reset request must be initiated.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset request was created. Used for audit trail and rate limiting purposes.

models.name: discussion_board_admin_audit_logs
models.description:
Immutable audit trail recording all administrative actions for security compliance and accountability.

Captures administrator-initiated operations including user bans and unbans, content moderation (article and comment deletions), section management (creation, modification, deletion), admin request approvals and rejections, and administrator grade changes (promotions and demotions). Each entry records the acting administrator, target entity, action type, optional reason, source IP address, and timestamp.

Records are append-only and preserved even when referenced entities (members, articles, comments, sections, admin requests) are deleted, ensuring complete audit history for compliance and forensic purposes.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who performed the action. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}. Set to null if the administrator account is deleted.

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: Target member for ban or unban actions. {@link discussion_board_members.id}. Set to null if the member account is deleted.

foreignFields.name: article_id
foreignFields.description: Target article for deletion actions. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}. Set to null when the article is permanently deleted.

foreignFields.name: comment_id
foreignFields.description: Target comment for removal actions. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}. Set to null when the comment is permanently deleted.

foreignFields.name: section_id
foreignFields.description: Target section for creation, modification, or deletion actions. {@link discussion_board_sections.id}. Set to null when the section is deleted.

foreignFields.name: admin_request_id
foreignFields.description: Target admin request for approval or rejection actions. {@link discussion_board_admin_requests.id}. Set to null if the request record is removed.

foreignFields.name: target_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Target administrator for promotion or demotion actions. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}. Set to null if the administrator account is deleted.

plainFields.name: action
plainFields.description: Type of administrative action performed. Values include: 'ban' for user bans, 'unban' for user unbans, 'promote' for admin grade promotion, 'demote' for admin grade demotion, 'delete_article' for article deletion, 'delete_comment' for comment removal, 'create_section' for section creation, 'update_section' for section modification, 'delete_section' for section deletion, 'approve_request' for admin request approval, 'reject_request' for admin request rejection.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Explanation or justification for the action. Required for ban actions to inform the banned user, and optional for other actions such as content deletion rationale or promotion/demotion justification.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Source IP address from which the administrative action was initiated, recorded for security auditing and forensic analysis.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrative action was recorded, used for chronological audit trail queries.

models.name: discussion_board_sections
models.description:
Thematic categories that organize articles into distinct discussion topics.

Sections serve as the primary navigation hierarchy for the discussion board, allowing users to discover articles by topic areas such as Politics, Economy, and Current Affairs. Each section has a unique name and descriptive text explaining what types of articles belong in that section.

Administrators create, edit, and delete sections. Section deletion is restricted to empty sections that contain no articles, ensuring referential integrity. All sections are publicly visible to all users including unauthenticated guests.

Key relationships:
- Created by {@link discussion_board_admins} (audit trail)
- Contains many {@link discussion_board_articles} (one-to-many)

foreignFields.name: created_by
foreignFields.description: Administrator who created this section. Required for audit trail per business rule [291] which mandates recording the creating administrator's identity. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Unique name identifying the topic area. Must be 1-100 characters, case-insensitive unique, and may contain alphanumeric characters, spaces, hyphens, and underscores. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Descriptive text explaining what types of articles belong in this section. Must be 1-500 characters. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed.

plainFields.name: sequence
plainFields.description: Display order for navigation and listing. Lower numbers appear first. Used for configurable section ordering in the navigation hierarchy.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was last modified. Updated when administrator edits the section name or description.

models.name: discussion_board_articles
models.description:
Main article entity representing the primary content unit where users share their perspectives on economic or political topics.

Each article has a title (headline), content (full text body), and creation timestamp. Articles belong to exactly one Section for topic categorization and have exactly one author (Member) who owns the content. Authors have exclusive rights to edit and delete their articles; administrators can delete any article.

Articles can have multiple tags (managed via {@link discussion_board_article_tags}) for flexible categorization, and multiple attachments (managed via {@link discussion_board_article_attachments}) including files and images. When an article is deleted, all associated comments and attachments are cascade deleted.

Title length: 1-200 characters. Content minimum: 20 characters.

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: The author (member) who created and owns this article. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

foreignFields.name: section_id
foreignFields.description: The section to which this article belongs for topic categorization. {@link discussion_board_sections.id}

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: The headline or subject of the article, summarizing the topic being discussed. Required field with length constraint of 1-200 characters. Displayed in article lists and detail views.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: The full body text containing the author's ideas and arguments on the topic. Required field with minimum length of 20 characters. Displayed on the article detail page for full reading.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The date and time when the article was published. Recorded automatically upon article creation and displayed to show when the article was posted.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: The date and time when the article was last modified. Updated automatically when the author edits the article content, title, or other attributes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for soft delete. When set, the article is removed from public view but retained in the database. Null for active articles.

models.name: discussion_board_tags
models.description:
Reusable tag master entity for flexible article categorization enabling cross-section topic discovery.

Tags provide user-defined categorization that complements section-based organization. Each tag is stored as free text with case-sensitive preservation, allowing organic content organization based on actual discussion topics.

Users can filter articles by one or more tags, search for articles by matching tag keywords, and discover related content across sections through tag associations. The unique name constraint prevents duplicate tags while supporting the many-to-many relationship with articles via the {@link discussion_board_article_tags} junction table.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Tag name as free text entered by the author. Stored case-sensitive with maximum 50 characters. Trimmed of leading and trailing whitespace. Used for article filtering and cross-section topic discovery.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the tag was first created. Records the moment a new tag is introduced to the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the tag record was last modified. Updated on any change to tag properties.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the tag was soft-deleted. Null for active tags. Set when a tag is deprecated without breaking existing article-tag associations.

models.name: discussion_board_article_tags
models.description:
Junction table establishing the many-to-many relationship between articles and tags for flexible multi-tag categorization and cross-section topic discovery.

Each record represents a single tag assignment to an article, enabling articles to have multiple tags and tags to be reused across many articles. The table enforces uniqueness to prevent duplicate tag assignments on the same article.

When an article is deleted, all its tag associations are automatically removed (cascade delete). Similarly, when a tag is deleted, all article associations for that tag are removed.

This subsidiary table is managed exclusively through the article entity - tags are added or removed during article creation and editing operations.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: The article that has this tag assigned. References {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_tag_id
foreignFields.description: The tag assigned to this article. References {@link discussion_board_tags.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this tag was assigned to the article. Used for audit trail and sorting tag assignments chronologically.

models.name: discussion_board_article_attachments
models.description:
File and image attachments associated with discussion board articles.

Each attachment provides supplementary content for articles, supporting both document files and images. Attachments are classified by type (file or image) to enable appropriate handling and display. When an article is deleted, all associated attachments are automatically removed.

Supported file formats: PDF, DOC, DOCX, XLS, XLSX, TXT, CSV (max 20MB per file).
Supported image formats: JPEG, PNG, GIF, WEBP (max 10MB per image).
Maximum 10 attachments per article with total size limit of 50MB.

Related entities:
- {@link discussion_board_articles}: Parent article that owns this attachment

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: The article this attachment belongs to. Each attachment is associated with exactly one article and is cascade deleted when the article is removed. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: Attachment type classification. Must be either 'file' for document attachments (PDF, DOC, DOCX, XLS, XLSX, TXT, CSV) or 'image' for image attachments (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WEBP). This classification determines appropriate handling and display behavior.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Original filename as uploaded by the user. Preserved for user reference and download display. Security-sensitive characters are sanitized while maintaining readability.

plainFields.name: extension
plainFields.description: File extension without the leading dot (e.g., 'pdf', 'jpg', 'png'). Used for format validation and content-type determination during download.

plainFields.name: size
plainFields.description: File size in bytes. Used for enforcing size limits (20MB max for files, 10MB max for images) and tracking storage usage. Also supports the 50MB total limit per article.

plainFields.name: path
plainFields.description: Storage path or URI where the attachment file is stored. Points to the actual file location in the storage system (local filesystem path or cloud storage URI).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was uploaded. Recorded during article creation or editing to track attachment history.

models.name: discussion_board_comments
models.description:
Member comments on articles with flat single-level structure.

Represents a registered member's written response to an article. Comments follow a flat,
single-level structure without nested replies, keeping discussions straightforward and
easy to follow. Each comment is permanently linked to its article and attributed to the
member who created it.

Comments are displayed in chronological order (oldest first) on articles and in user
profiles. Authors can modify their own comment content while preserving the original
creation timestamp. Administrators can delete any comment for moderation purposes.
When an article is deleted, all associated comments are cascade deleted.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link discussion_board_articles} as the commented article
- Belongs to {@link discussion_board_members} as the comment author

Business constraints:
- Content must be 10-10,000 characters
- No nested replies allowed (flat structure only)
- Comments from banned users remain visible with their attribution
- Cascade deleted when parent article is removed

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: The article this comment belongs to. Required association - every comment must be linked to exactly one article. Cascade deleted when the parent article is removed. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: The member who authored this comment. Required association - every comment must have an identified author. Comments from banned members remain visible with their display name attribution. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: The text content of the comment representing the member's opinion, question, or feedback. Must be between 10 and 10,000 characters. Empty or whitespace-only content is rejected. Content is stored and displayed exactly as submitted, subject to administrator moderation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was created. Used for chronological ordering (oldest first). Preserved even after comment edits - no separate edited timestamp is maintained.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was last updated. Updated when the author modifies the comment content.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was soft-deleted. Set when either the author or an administrator removes the comment. Null for active comments.

models.name: discussion_board_admin_requests
models.description:
Administrator privilege elevation requests submitted by members seeking admin status.

Represents a formal application process where members submit requests with a written reason for administrative privileges. Super administrators review pending requests and approve or reject them. The status lifecycle is: pending (awaiting review) → approved (user becomes regular admin) or rejected (user remains member). The system maintains complete history of all requests for audit purposes.

Key relationships:
- Requester: {@link discussion_board_members.id} - member who submitted the request
- Reviewer: {@link discussion_board_admins.id} - super admin who reviewed (null if pending)

Business rules:
- Only one pending request per member at any time
- Rejected requests allow resubmission
- Approved requests grant regular administrator privileges immediately
- Complete history preserved for audit

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: The member who submitted this administrator privilege request. References {@link discussion_board_members.id}.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: The super administrator who reviewed and decided on this request. Null while request is pending. References {@link discussion_board_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The written explanation provided by the requesting member explaining why they should be granted administrator privileges. Required field - request submission fails if empty or whitespace.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the administrator request. Lifecycle: pending (awaiting review) → approved (granted admin status) or rejected (user remains member). Valid values: 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected'. Status transitions are one-way only - approved/rejected requests cannot change status.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the admin request was submitted by the member.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the request was last modified (e.g., status changed from pending to approved/rejected).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for soft deletion. Admin request records are preserved for audit purposes even after deletion.

uniqueIndexes.description: Ensures only one request per status per member (prevents duplicate pending requests while allowing multiple approved/rejected records for audit history).

plainIndexes.description: Optimizes queries for pending requests that need super admin review.

models.name: discussion_board_admin_request_histories
models.description:
Audit trail preserving the complete history of admin request status transitions.

Each record captures a point-in-time state change for an administrator privilege request, including the new status, the super administrator who performed the action (if applicable), and the timestamp of the change. This enables historical tracking of the request lifecycle from submission through approval or rejection.

Relationships:
- Belongs to {@link discussion_board_admin_requests} as the request being tracked
- Reviewer references {@link discussion_board_admins} (the super administrator who approved/rejected)

Business Rules:
- Initial 'pending' status has null reviewer (set on request creation)
- 'approved' or 'rejected' status records include the reviewing super admin
- Records are append-only and never modified after creation

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_admin_request_id
foreignFields.description: The admin request whose status change is being recorded. {@link discussion_board_admin_requests.id}

foreignFields.name: reviewer_id
foreignFields.description: The super administrator who reviewed and changed the request status. Null for initial 'pending' status when the request is first created. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: The status of the admin request at this point in time. Valid values: 'pending' (awaiting review), 'approved' (accepted by super admin), 'rejected' (declined by super admin).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this history record was created, marking when the status change occurred.

models.name: discussion_board_administrator_grade_histories
models.description:
Audit trail of administrator grade changes recording promotions to super administrator and demotions to regular administrator.

This table captures grade change events performed by super administrators outside the admin request workflow. When a super administrator directly promotes a regular administrator to super administrator grade, or demotes another super administrator to regular administrator grade, the action is recorded here with complete audit information.

The table preserves the complete history of all grade changes including the target administrator, the acting super administrator who performed the action, the action type, the previous and new grades, and the timestamp. This supports compliance requirements and administrative oversight of privilege changes.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator whose grade was changed. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}. This is the target of the promotion or demotion action.

foreignFields.name: acted_by
foreignFields.description: The super administrator who performed the grade change action. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}. Only super administrators can promote or demote other administrators.

plainFields.name: action
plainFields.description: The type of grade change action performed. Valid values are 'promotion' (regular to super) or 'demotion' (super to regular). This field categorizes the administrative action for filtering and reporting.

plainFields.name: previous_grade
plainFields.description: The administrator's grade before this change. Valid values are 'regular' for regular administrators or 'super' for super administrators. This preserves the state before the action for audit trail completeness.

plainFields.name: new_grade
plainFields.description: The administrator's grade after this change. Valid values are 'regular' for regular administrators or 'super' for super administrators. This records the resulting state after the action.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the grade change action was performed. This is the audit record creation time and should not be modified after initial creation.
